newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina won't bust budget for elections - minister.
newsitem.headline: Argentina won't bust budget for elections - minister.

text.p: The Argentine government will not depart from its 1997 budget constraints to cede to the pressure of mid-term elections in October, said Economy Minister Roque Fernandez in an interview published Monday.
"Although we know this is a political year, we will not do anything that is not budgeted and planned," Fernandez told La Nacion newspaper.
The Argentine Congress has sanctioned a 1997 budget deficit of $3.4 billion -- higher than the $3.0 billion deficit sought by the government and agreed on by the International Monetary Fund.
The shortfall for 1996 is expected to be about $6.0 billion, or 2.0 percent of the country's gross domestic product.

The Peronist government of President Carlos Menem faces a tough election challenge this year. Menem was re-elected with a sweeping 50 percent of the vote as recently as May 1995. But political analysts are predicting the Peronists will lose their majority in Congress, though they will still have more seats than any other party.

They cite Argentina's high 17.3 percent unemployment rate as one of the main causes of Peronist unpopularity -- something Fernandez recognized, saying "unemployment is the big enemy to beat, more than the fiscal situation."
